title: Magic Positional Array Indexing (Obscuring Structures)
pattern: Using raw arrays or tuples and accessing elements by magic hardcoded numeric indexes to represent structured data entities with distinct sub-attributes.
why_bad: The knowledge of positional layout is duplicated everywhere the collection is processed. If the array layout changes, all lookup points must be updated, risking silent data corruption.
detection: Multiple expressions indexing numeric literals (e.g., `cell[0]`, `cell[1]`) on a raw homogeneous array to perform semantic computations.
counterexample: Mathematical matrices, coordinate planes, or standard linear geometry vectors where indices directly represent mathematical dimensions. `Context-dependent`.
source: *Practical Object-Oriented Design in Ruby*, Chapter 2, "Obscuring References" (p. 24).
